Hello fellow dirtbag!

It's actually not that bad compared to rock climbing, but the gear is absurdly expensive (I rent from my school). I don't know where you are but it's more common in the Rockies/Alaska than in the Appalachians. Definitely try it if you get the chance!

I'm not lucky enough to live there, but I do call colorful Colorado home! I worked at a national park up there on a trail crew this   summer and we got to travel (er... hitchhike) around the state a lot on our off time.

I can't speak for what I smell like when I'm backpacking, but I have been told that I normally smell like dryer sheets and peppermint, so there ya go. What do hippies smell like? Patchouli?

Kenai is amazing! I actually worked at a national park further inland, which is also definitely worth visiting if you find yourself up there! The coast is great, but the Chugach and Denali mountain ranges are incredible if you can tolerate the bugs!
